utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any cross-examination? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This witness calls for no cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. We do have a couple of questions for this witness, and with your permission we should like to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stojanovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We listened to your answers yesterday and we have read your statement, the one that you gave to the OTP on the 27th of November, 2002, and on the 1st of December, 2002. But there are certain things that have remained unclear, and I would like to ask you for your help. Let me just ask you to wait a little before you proceed with giving your answer, because we have to be mindful of the interpretation because we speak the same language. So please bear in mind, just a brief pause between question and answer. Thank you. In the statement -- or rather, in your testimony yesterday and in your statement given in 2002, you said that you were mobilised on the 20th of May, 1992, and that formally speaking, the commander of your unit was Mihajlo Galic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know I was mobilised into a detachment as far as I recall, and that was my first commander, the first commander I was assigned to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you given any war assignment in that unit? Were you deployed on one of the positions of that unit for a while before you were demobilised?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean for a while? For the entire period of the war or ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in the period prior to withdrawal from the unit before you went back to the local commune. I'm interested in the year of 1992. Were you ever deployed at the frontline or at any other position, and if so, where?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I withdrew from the unit, I was part of that unit. I was mobilised until the 16th of March, 1996. So from the 20th of May, 1992, until 1996. So throughout that period of time, I would always respond to any invitation or order by the commander, except in some exceptional circumstances when I was not available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where were you deployed in 1992?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. I believe -- well, the siege of the battalion was in Kiseljak, and it was in 1992 so it must have been Mr. Galic who summoned us to report to the unit before the battalion was deployed. Now I remember. At one point it became a battalion, the 23rd Battalion. So from August onwards, the battalion was deployed on the separation line between Pilica and Teocak. My assignment at the time was in the rear of the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that your unit was deployed as far as Teocak, is it true that it was up to the point which is called Tursanovo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the area between Pilica and Teocak, so I believe this was Tursanovo Brdo and a very small hamlet, Krcina [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that the furthest right point of the area which was held by the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't spend a lot of time there, but that should have been the case I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you will agree with me when I say that you were the right-wing, the furthermost right point which was held by the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That would be the location on the map.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The members of the battalion, were most of them mobilised conscripts from the local area, from Pilica, Lokanj, and Sijes [phoen]. Did you have any specific task in that unit?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly. I was in the kitchen, in the rear, that is at least how I was registered on the -- on the schedule. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you were already president of the Pilica local commune at that time in 1992?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when you were elected president of the local commune.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was on the 11th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you that in the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2002, you stated that you were president of the local community from the 20th of April 1992. Today you're saying that you were elected on the 11th of May. What is correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that we didn't understand each other at the time. On the 11th of April, I was a member of the council of the local commune, but I was active in that council even before that in 1990 and 1991. So it's possible that a mistake occurred, that there was a misunderstanding. It was on the 11th of May, as far as I can recall at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The way I understand was that you were given an opportunity to re-read the statement when you arrived here in The Hague and that you entered certain corrections in your statement in handwriting, that you corrected everything that you thought was -- had been incorrectly translated or worse, erroneous?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I did so on the last page of the statement taken in 1995. I didn't have anything in particular to say in connection with 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But from what I can see from the statement, you entered certain corrections in respect of 1992.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, as far as I was able to understand, that's possible, but only partially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't understand. What do you mean when you say "only partially"? Did you or did you not enter any corrections in the statement in which you said that you were elected president of the local community on the 20th of April?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't pay much attention to the dates. I was concerned with words rather than the dates. So as far as I can recall at this point, those are the dates that I remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is possible that the statement that you gave contains other mistakes that you failed to notice and did not correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could observe yesterday, there were certain problems with the chronology of the events -- I mean, as we discussed it during the testimony and as it was described in the statement, and it was a little bit confusing for me, I must admit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I do agree with you, Mr. Petrovic, and this is exactly why I think that it is possible that there are still mistakes in the statement. So if you should notice something that is not correct in your statement during our conversation, please let me know. So it is not correct that on the 20th of April, 1992, as it is stated in the statement that you signed, that you were elected president of the local commune. The correct answer is the 11th of May, 1992. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 11-day [as interpreted] difference -- I mean, I cannot recall at this point when it was exactly, and I also know -- I mean you said that I gave another statement on another occasion, and I don't understand what exactly you have in mind, if you can explain this to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I mentioned the statement, or rather, the record of the statement that we received yesterday, which reflects your conversation with the OTP on the 30th of November this year, that is when you arrived here in the Netherlands. So this is the other statement.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Now I understand what you meant. I was thinking of other statements, the ones taken in 2002.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So we will use both statements, the one that you gave on the 27th of November, 2002, and the Prosecutor's note of your interview of the 30th of November, 2003. I believe that you stated that you had had several breaks of service in your unit because you were busy at the local commune as the president of the local commune. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, were you the president or a member of the SDS at the time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any specific function or did you hold any specific office within the SDS?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was just a member of the Zvornik chapter of SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you become a member of the Zvornik SDS board -- a member of the municipal assembly in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me remind you that the assembly was elected in 1990, right after the first multi-party elections. Were you an SDS deputy at that time or did you become the deputy only later on?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I became the deputy later on, subsequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, so I am referring to the period between April and May 1992, were you also an SDS member at the Zvornik Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe it was only later in the end of 1992 or maybe beginning of 1993. I don't know exactly, but I'm sure that I was not a deputy during that period of time that you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to the results of the elections in the Pilica local commune, did the SDS hold power in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but let me finish the previous question. The government was not formed according to the multi-party election results. It was the citizens who proposed candidates for the local commune assembly, regardless of their party membership as required by the statute of the local commune. So the deputies of the local commune assembly are elected directly by the citizens, according to the proposals or nominations. So practically speaking, there were no elections for local commune assembly deputies, and they were not based on political party membership.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you will agree with me if I say that the local commune assembly elected you, a member of the SDS, as the president of the local commune?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But let me explain. The assembly was established at the meeting of the citizens, and then it was only after the assembly has been established that the members of the assembly can elect their president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they elected you as a member of SDS on the 11th of May, 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the president of the local commune council. And after the war broke out, the assembly stopped working. So it was the council of the local commune that is in charge of the work of the local commune if the assembly is no longer functioning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after the breakout of the war, it was the local commune council that was established, and it was constituted as the local Crisis Staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it was first the Territorial Defence staff prior to the relevant instruction of the council, that is, prior to the outbreak of the war, we had the so-called Territorial Defence council. And the Territorial Defence was under the control of the Ministry of Defence, as was the civilian protection department. The Territorial Defence had its competencies and its responsibilities, and the council members had their responsibilities, but that did not mean that they could not be members of the Territorial Defence staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you also elected president of the Crisis Staff in Pilica during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What period of time are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: April/May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Between the 20th of April and the 30th of April, the president of the Crisis Staff was another gentleman, and I became president on the 30th of November, as far as I can recall at this point.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 3rd of July, 1992, you were the president of the local commune council. Now, to your local commune, a group of people was brought from the technical school in Karakaj. The Muslims in question had been captured in the village of Djulici.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is how I understood it to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, did you have any particular tasks with regard to these prisoners or whatever you wish to call them, the prisoners that had been brought from the village of Djulici in 1992?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These people, while they were detained in Djulici, did you organise distribution of bread to the Pilica community centre?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean "while they were detained in Djulici"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. There's been a misunderstanding. While the people from Djulici were detained in the Pilica community centre, did you organise distribution of bread for them during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on one occasion, but not me personally. I had asked a number of citizens to buy bread, and I think I myself went to buy some bread in the local shop in Pilica as well. The next day I went to the Territorial Defence to see Mr. Marko Pavlovic in order to have the proper food distribution organised, which indeed happened two days later through the security service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you ask Marko Pavlovic who those people were, what kind of prisoners they were?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't ask any such question. I didn't inquire about the nature of these detainees. My main concern was to ask Marko Pavlovic to organise distribution of food for them, and I wanted someone else to take care of them because it was summertime, this was in a densely populated area, and I was afraid of an outbreak of epidemics, in view of the conditions that were highly improper for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did Marko Pavlovic tell you on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that he would try to organise food distribution, to see what we could -- would do with them, what should be done with them, and that the security service would be informed about the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you that they were not your responsibility?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, something to that effect. I couldn't quote his words, but he drew my attention to the fact that there was a security service which would be in charge of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement you mentioned a name, Jovo Ivanovic. Is it true that Jovo Ivanovic during that period of time in 1992 was vice-president of the Zvornik municipality War Presidency?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the vice-president of the War Presidency in Zvornik? I was never aware of the fact that he was the vice-president of any War Presidency. I'm not sure what period of time you're talking about. I know that there was a War Presidency in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In May 1992, what was Jovo Ivanovic responsible for? What kind of work did he perform?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I know that he was a deputy, peoples' deputy in May 1992. As to what specific duties he had at the time, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he also a deputy on the basis of his membership of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in the SDS before, too. When I became a deputy in 1992/1993, he was already a deputy. As far as I remember, I think he was the president of the executive committee of the Municipal Assembly of Zvornik before the war, as far as I can remember. I remember that he was the president of the executive committee before the war, but when the war broke out, I didn't follow this. I don't know what position he held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we say the president of the executive committee, would you agree with me that the executive committee had executive authority in the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Before the war, they did a bridge and a request was sent to the executive committee. I remember that the signature for the construction of the bridge was Jovo Ivanovic's. That was before the war. And during the war, I can remember that the director was Pilica/Zvornik company and Vitika [phoen].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1992, are you aware that at the level of the Zvornik municipality a Crisis Staff was formed?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As part of the Crisis Staff, was the president of the executive committee of the municipality -- of Zvornik municipality, a member of the Crisis Staff by virtue of his position?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure that's a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dragan Obrenovic from that period, who was later the deputy commander of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have known Dragan Obrenovic. I knew him for a few months during that period while he was the commander of some unit. I didn't know him personally. I knew some of my friends. I had some friends who were in the reserve force of the JNA, and they said that Dragan Obrenovic was the commander, but I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that as the commander of the mechanised battalion in 1992, while he was in Zvornik he participated in the work of the municipality of Zvornik Crisis Staff, together with Jovo Ivanovic?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware that he was in the Crisis Staff. I was down one occasion, perhaps. I don't know what position he held. I can't remember whether I saw him. Perhaps I did, but I didn't know him personally. I don't know the composition of the Crisis Staff. As to what positions people held, well I heard that some people were members of the Crisis Staff, but I didn't hear that this was the case for Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday in response to a question from the Prosecution, you said that you knew Dragan Jokic from that period. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew Dragan Jokic towards the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993. We worked on a stretch of road, and I think in 1994 he worked on another stretch of road in the Pilica municipality. But in 1994, I cooperated to a lesser extent because he had a man who was taking care of that particular stretch of road. And then Dragan Jokic's unit and the engineer unit was involved in that work as far as I can remember the dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you conclude with regard to Dragan Jokic? What sort of a person was he?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday I said that I had very positive memories of him. I cooperated in a very correct manner with him, especially when building roads, when the municipality provided fuel, transport, the quality of the work when constructing the roads was very good in the municipality. And we were very grateful at the time to Mr. Jokic. That was the first time we built such roads in the municipality by using that system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you socialised, when you knew him, when you would meet him, did you ever notice in the war conditions, in those conditions of war, that he manifested signs of nationalism of religious or national intolerance?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even think about that. We never discussed the subject. Everything mostly concerned tasks, and the tasks I had to the municipality -- well, these are things that we discussed. We didn't discuss other matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you never heard any such story from him? Could you just confirm this. Is your answer yes?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The microphone was not working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to conclude this series of questions within another question. Yesterday, if this date is correct, because it is not in accordance with your statement, on the 14th, 15th, and 16th, as you mentioned Sunday, you said that you were at home. And on the 17th when you came to the municipality. Mr. Petrovic, during that period from the 14th to the 18th of July, 1995, did you see Dragan Jokic personally in Branjevo, Pilica, anywhere?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the dates are concerned, in my statement it says the 12th of June. It has to be the 12th of July. I know it was about Petrov Dan. I don't know whether it was the 11th or 12th or the 14th, 15th, 16th, I don't know. I'm not sure of the exact date, but to answer your question, I didn't see Mr. Jokic anywhere, apart from the conversation that we had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't see him, but did you hear that during that period -- did you hear anyone say that Dragan Jokic was in Branjevo during that period?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never mentioned this. No, I never said such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll just return to this conversation now, because the Defence, Mr. Petrovic, is claiming that on that day you didn't have such a conversation with Dragan Jokic, who is present here. And by putting questions to you and presenting you with pieces of evidence, we shall attempt to determine whether you did or didn't have such a conversation. If I have understood you correctly, Mr. Petrovic, it was only on the basis of his voice that you concluded that you were speaking to Dragan Jokic. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, it is important for you to wait for the interpreter to finish and then to answer the question. Thank you. Because this is a linguistic barrier that we have to bridge. Would you allow for the possibility that, given the time that has passed from the time that you spoke to the person whom you say was Jokic and investigators, is it possible that the person on the other side was someone else?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after so much time -- I'm thinking about that. I know that I discussed this subject and that the duty officer, that's how he presented himself, as Dragan Jokic. Perhaps there was a variation, a difference. I wasn't there personally. I wasn't on the site, so I wasn't able to see Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as you did not see him personally, you only heard him, you allow for the possibility that it might have been someone else. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He presented himself as the duty officer, Dragan Jokic. That is how he introduced himself at all times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. We will now try to follow the chronology of events to see whether we are right or not. In your statement, you said that on that morning, or on that day - we won't mention the exact date because we have a problem - you said that you met Slavko Peric. And here in the translation, it says that this was a person on the staff. Can you please explain to us who Slavko Peric is and what duties he had at the time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I corrected this yesterday. We didn't use the term "staff." We said -- we used the terms battalion and brigade. Slavko Peric was someone from the battalion. What was it called at the time? The 1st Infantry Battalion. And I think -- what was his position called? I think he was a security officer in the battalion, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I say that Slavko Peric was the assistant -- was the deputy commander of the battalion for intelligence and security affairs in the 1st or Pilica Battalion, would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if that's the name of that position, yes. I don't know exactly. I know that he had something to do with security in the battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that at that time he held a high military position, a high military rank in that battalion as a security officer?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll probably agree with you. Assuming he was the assistant commander, he must have had such -- he probably had such responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say further on in your statement that you asked Slavko Peric what the problem was. And he said that from the headquarters, from the command of the brigade, he had received a telegram, and that some prisoners would arrive. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say where those prisoners would arrive?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said I don't know anything. I have to prepare the premises. I have to prepare some facilities. I asked where. He said: I don't know anything. I have to prepare the facilities, get the facilities ready.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he say which facilities where he had to prepare?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't. But my conclusion was that that area was Biskurija [phoen] near the school, was near the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean the school that we call Kula in the village? Can you tell us about what time it was on that day.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I can remember, it was sometime between 11.00 -- between 10.00 and 11.00, something like that. Perhaps a little later. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this conversation take place?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the road in front of the school, near the entrance to the schoolyard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you organised this meeting or was it accidental?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the answer, the interpreter did not hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the interpreter did not hear the answer. Witness, would you please repeat the answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We met accidentally, by chance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the sake of the transcript, in response to the question how you met, whether you had agreed to meet, whether it had been organised, or whether it was an accidental meeting, the witness replied that they had met by chance in front of the school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I don't think it's necessary to ask, but correct me if I'm wrong. Peric, Slavko, is from Pilica, from the same village as you. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that Slavko Peric gave statements to the investigators on two occasions?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever spoken to Slavko Peric about what was to happen, that you were being summoned to come to The Hague or did he speak to you about his testimony?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a few days ago we spoke about the fact that I had received a letter, a summons from The Hague. He said that he had also given a statement. I didn't know that he had given a statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he mention that conversation at all, the fact that you met by chance in front of the school?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't mention that. He didn't speak about that subject.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you be surprised if I told you now that in the statement of Slavko Peric's, in front of me, he didn't mention the fact that he spoke to you about 10.00 on that day?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wouldn't be a surprise. Perhaps he couldn't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that it is possible that Slavko Peric might not have mentioned your accidental meeting?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it was insignificant, so he didn't mention it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Petrovic. If I try to explain this, Slavko Peric, and you say that he held a fairly high military position at the time, he informed you about what was going to happen. The question is: Why, in spite of that fact, you wanted to go and check with the brigade commander to see what was going to happen?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because at that time, Slavko quickly said: I received a telegram and prisoners will arrive. And he went somewhere else. I went to check this out, because throughout the wartime period, although Slavko is a relative of mine, we weren't on good terms. He didn't say this to me in a friendly manner, and I couldn't really believe him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why weren't you on good terms? Because your political views diverged or some other reason?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't feel a difference in political opinion, a difference in political opinion, but because of the position he had, there were problems with the army and perhaps it was his duty to conduct himself in a certain manner. If I told him why I hadn't joined the army -- or I hadn't come to the army, he didn't accept it, and he became angry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I conclude on this basis that you are saying that you didn't believe what Slavko Peric told you?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that that is the reason for which you wanted to check the information that you had received from a woman whom you had also met by chance in the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- no, not in the brigade command. I didn't meet the woman in the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't even say that.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is: Am I correct when I say that the reason for which you wanted to check this in the brigade command, you wanted to check the allegations that you had heard from a woman you had met by chance, the reason for this is that you did not believe the information that Slavko Peric provided you with, Slavko Peric, the duty officer in the Pilica Battalion?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the information that the woman provided with me was information I received before Slavko Peric mentioned this. When Slavko Peric told me about this, I didn't -- I wasn't completely distrustful. I believed it to an extent, but he didn't go into details. He didn't explain it to me. So I wanted to take the opportunity to check the facts in the brigade and to see if it would be possible to do something so that the prisoners didn't come to Pilica. That's why I tried to establish contact with the brigade commander, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, how did you go to Sepak village?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a car of an acquaintance. Perhaps it was Niko Micic but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you didn't find Jovo Ivanovic at home. And that at your request a relative of his allowed you to use his telephone. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Something like that happened as far as I can remember. He was doing something in the yard, perhaps working on the fence. Jovo Ivanovic wasn't there; he came later as far as I can remember. So that's what I chose to do. I remember that we used a wireless phone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I haven't understood you correctly -- very well now. You are saying it's possible that Jovo Ivanovic came when you were speaking to the brigade command [Realtime transcript read in error "commander"]?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that, as far as I can recall that event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that relative, did he listen to the conversation with the brigade command [Realtime transcript read in error "commander"] or were you on your own at the time?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps we were sitting at some table in the yard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the relative standing there, too, while you were speaking?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember. He was somewhere nearby. I can't remember where that relative was exactly. He was somewhere on the grounds. I can't describe where he was now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell this Trial Chamber --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt. I note in the transcript it refers to brigade commander and I believe the question related to the brigade command and I believe that needs to be corrected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think that is on page 20, line 14.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Line 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, would you please check it. There are two places in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honours. So I don't think anything will be in dispute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question was: When you spoke to the brigade command, not when you spoke to the brigade commander, on that occasion was that relative present? Just for the sake of the transcript, you cannot state with certainty whether he was in the immediate -- whether he was right by you, but he was somewhere in the vicinity. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, that relative -- I don't know whether Jovo was somewhere there at the time. I know we spoke about this matter, but I don't know whether he listened to the conversation. We discussed the subject. We discussed phoning the brigade command. But as to whether he heard the conversation or perhaps -- or whether he went off somewhere else, I can't remember right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But can you tell us and can you assist us in trying to determine the facts, what was the name of Jovo Ivanovic's relative who was present when you spoke to the brigade command?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember now. Perhaps it was Jevto Simic from Pilica, but I don't know whether he came with me or whether he was already there or was someone else there, too, I can't remember. But Jevto Simic is my relative. Perhaps at the time he was working for him; that is a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I have understood you correctly, perhaps he came with you from Sepak to Pilica to work at Jovo Ivanovic's?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that he came with me at the time, or perhaps he was already there. I'm not sure whether he came with us or whether he was already there. As far as I can remember, I think that he was in the yard at the time, but I think that he was doing some work on the fence around the yard and there were other workers who were there, but I can't remember who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could he have heard that conversation?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was, you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was near -- well, it's possible he was nearby.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would I be correct to say that the conversation you had with someone in the Zvornik Brigade command, would it be correct to say that no one heard that conversation, including Jevto Simic who was nearby?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we commented on this matter before I phoned and afterwards. Perhaps we spoke about it in a group -- spoke about who I had to phone and what had to be discussed, as far as I can remember the event.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason for your travel to Sepak from Pilica to make a phone call?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no telephone in Pilica, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry. I don't understand you. You cannot remember whether it worked or not?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the reason why it didn't work. I know we went to Sepak because it was impossible to phone from Pilica, but I don't know the reason why the lines were down. We often went to the post office there during the war, because the lines were often down during the war. And this is what I had in mind when I declared in my statement that the telephone was not working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's exactly what I was going to ask you about, Mr. Petrovic. When you say that the telephone was not working, are you referring to Pilica, to the nearby households, the catering businesses, or to the telephone in your office?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that the main switchboard in Pilica was a very old one, and I believe that some lines were down and some were not. I know that one part of Pilica did have telephone working and the other did not for a longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where Milijan's Cafe is located in relation to your office?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the road towards Bijeljina, some hundred metres away, further down the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean it is about a hundred metres away from your office?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far from your office is the house of Jovo Ivanovic in Sepak?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 3 to 4 kilometres, maybe more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether during that period of time, that is in mid-July, there was a telephone line at Milijan's Cafe?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot remember. I know there was a phone, but I'm not sure if the phone was working. There had been a phone before the war; I know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I told you that in July 1995 there was a telephone bill issued to this catering business for telephone services carried out in the past period?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, because sometimes the lines would be down for three to four days, sometimes they would be working for a couple of days. I know that when the lines were down, we would go to the next nearby local commune to use the phone. So it is possible. I know that the reason why I went there was because the phone wasn't working in Pilica. I know that we spent a year or two in Pilica without a telephone -- or rather, that we were having problems with telephone lines during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I say that it is more logical for you to go to Milijan's Cafe which was only 100 metres away to try and make a phone call and to check what Slavko Peric had told you than to go to Sepak to perform such a conversation?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you. It is more logical, but maybe at that time I knew that the telephone in Milijan's Cafe was not working. Maybe I was not sure. Maybe if the telephone was not working on that day, I decided to go there. I mean, I didn't have information, exact information, as to which telephone in which household was working on that particular day. I'm not ruling out the possibility that on that day it was working in my office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was working, sir, but what I'm trying to say that it is possible also that Jovo Ivanovic's telephone was not working either. I'm just saying that instead of covering the distance of 100 metres, you decided to go to the nearby village which was 3 to 4 kilometres away and to make a phone call from there?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I think about that, it was more -- would have been more logical, but I also remember that I never used the telephone in Milijan's Cafe. It was not my habit from calling from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We believe that if you went to Jovo Ivanovic, Mr. Pero, it was because you wanted to check with Jovo who at the time was a member of the War Presidency, because we are talking about 1995, he was one of the prominent SDS leaders, you wanted to see with him what was going on and what you were to expect. Am I right or not?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the War Presidency, I think that it was Mr. Jovan Mitrovic who was the president of the War Presidency at the time. I was not aware of the members of the War Presidency, and I didn't know that Jovo Ivanovic was a member of the War Presidency. I had never heard anything to that effect and I was not informed of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you will agree with me -- after all, you said that you were both members of the Zvornik Municipal Assembly on behalf of SDS, and that at the time you knew that Jovo Ivanovic was the president of the executive council in 1992. And in 1995 you said there was also a War Presidency in the municipality of Zvornik. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but again I'm not aware of who the members of the War Presidency were. Nobody informed me of that. I only know that Jovan Mitrovic was a member of the War Presidency. I never inquired of the membership of the War Presidency. There was no need for me to know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have the members of the presidency, I do not want to insist on that. All I want is to put to you the reason why you went to Sepak. It was not -- I was not interested into the members of the War Presidency; this is not important for us at the moment. But is it possible that it was for those reasons that you went to Jovo Ivanovic's house, that you wanted to talk about what was to happen in view of the large number of prisoners that was arriving and you wanted Jovo Ivanovic to tell you what to do?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree that Jovo Ivanovic did have some very important functions within the municipality, but I don't know whether he was a member of the War Presidency. It's possible that I did. Maybe that was the reason why I want to the house of that person. There is certain logic to that, I agree. As to what specific function at that particular moment he had, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely, Mr. Petrovic. That is exactly what we are trying to say, and that was the reason why you went to Sepak. And that was the reason why you needed Jovo Ivanovic to tell you what would happen. Before I show you a Prosecutor's exhibit, let me ask you: Do you remember what time it was?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it could have been one hour after the conversation that I had had with Slavko, as far as I can recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So between 12.00, half past 12.00 -- I mean the conversation with the Zvornik Brigade command from Sepak?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me conclude with this topic. You testified yesterday that you had first talked to the switchboard at the brigade, and it was the switchboard people who put you through to the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That should have been the case. I -- I must have gone through the switchboard. I told you all the details that I knew about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that this was not necessarily the case, that you are not sure, which is an acceptable answer. So you're not sure if you first talked to the duty officer or someone at the -- or that you first talked to someone at the switchboard who then put you through to the duty officer? You're not sure who it was?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember how exactly it went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's fine with me. That is a perfectly acceptable answer, in view of the lapse of time. But do you abide by your statement that you first talked to the person who was on duty at the switchboard and then you wanted to be put through to the duty officer, which is what happened?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess. I'm not sure that's how they worked. I remember that I called them. What the procedure was, I don't remember. But you're trying to make me say that I don't remember. It is possible that I have forgotten.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I do understand if you have forgotten. That is certainly an acceptable and frank answer. If you say: I don't remember, that is also fine with us. These are really very important issues and we have to be precise. I want to hear from you that possibility, that that was not necessarily the case.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure. What I know was that I was eventually told that I should not busy myself with that, that that was not my task. And I wouldn't have known that if I had not called. I don't know. It's possible that I had just picked up the receiver.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Precisely. You knew that Dragan Jokic was the duty officer, so that's why you concluded that it was him who said that this was none of your business, that those were war prisoners?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know that before. I may have known later, after I talked to Dragan Jokic and after he told me that I should not interfere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, you are not sure that the man with whom -- you're not sure that the man with whom you talked is precisely the person present here in the court, this Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I don't know any other proof at this point. This is what I remember. If you have any other evidence. But from what I know the only conclusion is that's how it went, that it was on that day that I learned that Dragan Jokic was the duty officer. And that is what we discussed during that conversation. He told me that this was not my concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, maybe this is a good moment for the break before we proceed with presenting the evidence that we have preferred. This is really the key moment of our cross-examination. Thank you for allowing me to complete this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I quite understand that, because since you said let's conclude on this topic, at least we have gone through two pages. But anyway, we'll have our break and we'll resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Witness, would you please speak a little bit louder and speak directly to the microphone, because during the break I was informed that the interpreters could not catch up with you. Thank you very much. Mr. Stojanovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we continue. Mr. Petrovic, on the 30th of November, you gave a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. Did they mention anything to you about the fact that the conversations that took place at the Zvornik Brigade command were being listened to by the members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you happen to hear from other sources that the conversation of the Zvornik Brigade were being intercepted?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may ask the assistance of the usher, please. I would like P229 to be distributed. I should actually like to show it to the witness so that we can hear his comment. I'm interested in page 2, which contains the text in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, I would like to draw your attention to the sentence before -- that appears before the names Zlatar, Zivanovic; Jokic, duty officer, on the 12th that is the frequency was not active between 11.30 and 2020.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So with your permission, Your Honour, I should like to ask my question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in accordance with the testimony of some BH army members which we had the opportunity of hearing, they testified before this Chamber how they went about the frequencies and how it was possible for to intercept your conversations -- or rather, the conversations on Channel 3. That was the frequency of the Zvornik Brigade command. Now, the time in question is 2128 [as interpreted] of this particular conversation. The BH army claim that the frequency was not active from 11.30 until 2020. Now, the way that I interpret this, Mr. Petrovic, is that between that period of time between half 11.00 and 20 minutes past 8.00 p.m., they were not able to intercept any telephone conversation that may have been -- that may have taken place at the Zvornik Brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: First of all, with all due respect, I don't think that Mr. Stojanovic's interpretation is necessarily accurate, nor is it relevant. And I don't think that he can put a question in this form to a witness. And I'm going to object to that question and ask that he not be permitted to pursue this line of questioning in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, so far as I know, I didn't hear the question yet. Maybe the question itself is quite relevant. Would you please allow Mr. Stojanovic to finish his question.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. I was under the impression that he had finished it, but I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think it's a statement just on his part. While the different parties may claim different things and have different interpretations. But you have to focus on the questions. I hope Mr. Stojanovic could ask a question so then we could see whether it is relevant or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But we will bear your objections in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm trying to establish the relevance of what the Prosecution is claiming as well as the relevance of what we claim. So if the Prosecution can rely on this evidence, I see no reason why it should not be verified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question for you, Mr. Petrovic, is as follows: Is it possible that between half past 11.00 and 20 minutes past 20 hours on the 14th of July, no conversation was intercepted. And you said that you made that call between 12.00 and half past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this date, the 14th of July. This does not accord with my recollection. The conversation, according to what I remember, should have taken place around the 12th of July, but again I'm not sure. This date, the 14th of July, doesn't really ring a bell. I don't know. I'm not sure that this took place after 11.30. It could have been sometime around 10.00. Again, I don't remember the exact hour, but the date doesn't look familiar, the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to be able to understand you completely. Are you trying to say that the conversation did not take place on the 14th or that the conversation did not take place between 12.00 and 12.30 on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my previous statements and according to my knowledge as far as the dates are concerned, the events we are talking about took place sometime before the 12th of July. And now I'm confused. I don't know where this date, the 14th of July, has come from. This doesn't mean that you're not right, but I'm not sure, once again, that this did not take place before 12.30. I'm not sure about the hours, at any rate. I can only approximate the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, for insisting, but let me try to clarify.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think, Mr. Petrovic, that the conversation that you discussed, just as you mentioned it in your statement, took place before St. Peter's Day, that is the 12th of July, or after the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened just prior to the arrival, but my recollection is that it took place sometime around the 12th of July. But it is also possible that it had taken place before the 12th of July. At least, this is the impression that I have at this point. You see the date here, but I know that it was one or two hours -- maybe three or four hours before the arrival of the prisoners that this conversation had taken place. And as far as I remember, it was during the morning hours. But I'm confused about the date. I really don't know what is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This really favours our position, and I would like to establish the truth. Dragan Jokic was not the duty officer in the Zvornik Brigade on the 12th and around that date. So if you insist that the conversation took place at that time, I'm not going to insist, but if you're now telling this Chamber that the conversation may have taken place on the 14th, then I have to insist. Because on the basis of that, it turns out that no one -- it follows that no one was able to intercept any conversation.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I really cannot remember the exact date. I said around Petrov Dan, St. Peter's Day, which is on the 12th of July. Whether it was a day before that or a day after that, I don't know. But in my statement, I said that it was on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us try this way: If I say that this was not on the 14th of July, but rather on the 12th of July or maybe before that day -- that date, would I be correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can remember, it should have been sometime around the 12th. I'm sorry, I cannot be more precise as far as the date is concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. I believe this is something that we can live with, as far as the date is concerned, because it is not disputed that on the 12th of July Dragan Jokic was not the duty officer at the Zvornik Brigade command. But let me ask you the following: What was your understanding of those prisoners of war? Did anyone mention the fact that they would be killed or whether any talks about the possibility of their being exchanged?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no reason for anyone to mention anything to that effect. My understanding was that it would turn out differently than it eventually did. I stated to the investigators of the OTP that that is what I believed, or rather, that the war year of 1995 was under some sort of military organisation. No one ever mentioned to me why these prisoners would be important.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, on the 14th of July, did anyone say anything to the effect that they would be killed?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Like I said, I never knew what would happen. No one ever told me anything about it, none before that, not at that time, not after that. It's not something that I was able to hear from someone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any talks about the exchange? Did anyone tell you that they were waiting to be exchanged?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never had any conversation with anyone to that effect. I was merely observing the events.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To follow-up on this, do you know that in the 1st Infantry Pilica Battalion, that is the 1st Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade, there was also Dusan Jokic, that he was a reserve officer and that he was with the mortar group?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me try to remember the name. Jokic, the mortar battery, I'm not sure. There may have been a man by that name, but in 1992 -- I cannot remember. What period are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm interested in the summer of 1995, July 1995.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any information about a mortar platoon at the time or a Dusan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Petrovic, let's return to the 15th. According to what you said yesterday, on that day, having been to the school, you decided to go to the municipality for the sake of organisation and the demobilisation of a soldier. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in response to a question from the Prosecution, you resolved the dilemma that you had or did not have and that was your statement that you gave when preparing for this trial on the 30th of November. I'd like to remind you that according to these notes that we have received, you stated that on the following morning, the day after the prisoners had been brought in, you went to Zvornik to deal with affairs that had to do with the local commune. As he was passing by the school, he saw buses that were parked there. There were prisoners in the school, et cetera. And yesterday you said that what had been recorded by the Prosecution was not correct. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I didn't hear the first question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct to say that on the 30th of November, you told the Prosecution that the morning after the prisoners had arrived you set off to Zvornik. You passed by the Kula school, and on that occasion you saw buses that were parked there and prisoners in the school. And then yesterday in the course of the examination-in-chief, you denied this. You said there was a misunderstanding and that that concerned the 14th -- and that on the 15th you hadn't passed by the Kula school. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday, as far as that event is concerned, I said that when I spoke to Slavko Peric, I went to the office. I went to Sepak. I returned from Sepak and went home to deal with some minor affairs. And on that day, I returned to the Kula school again. I think that that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that on the following day before heading for Zvornik, you didn't pass by the Kula school?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I didn't pass by, and if I did, it was in a car. Because I took different routes. But on the first day when I went home on that day, I returned home, I didn't see anyone. When I returned the second time, perhaps there was a misunderstanding in the translation and it seemed to be on the second day. But the second time I returned was on that day when I was in Sepak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to what we have received and the Prosecution has pointed this out to you, too, it says that this happened on the following day, the following morning. Well, I just want to clarify this. What is correct? The first statement given to the Prosecution or the second one given to the Prosecution or what you stated yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my second statement, the second time I returned home, I saw that, that's probably what I said. The second time I returned home, I saw that. I thought that referred to my second return, but on that day I passed by on two occasions, once when there were no prisoners and the second time when there were prisoners there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can I conclude what is stated in the statement, or rather, in the notes, is not correct, the record of the discussion with the Prosecution on the 30th of November?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's correct to say that I passed a second time, but it doesn't mean on another day. The second time I passed by, I saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand you. You just want to say that it was on that day that you passed by the school and saw the prisoners, and that was when you passed by on the second day?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the second time I passed by, and perhaps it seems as if it was on another day, on the second day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It has been recorded here that that was on another day, after you had spent the night at home and went to Zvornik, that that happened on another day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I think we've been over this a number of times now. It's getting quite repetitive. The witness has made it clear what his answer is and I'm going to suggest respectfully that we should perhaps move on from this point. It is getting repetitive and rather confusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so, Mr. Stojanovic. And especially I could not understand the question you asked just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I won't ask any more questions about this matter. I think we have solved the -- resolved the matter. But I want to say this, and this is the purpose of the question: That this witness has changed the statement that he gave to the Prosecution on the 30th of July. He did that yesterday, and he said that this was correct and we have seen that that was the case. He gave a statement on 2002, and then he changed it on the 30th of November, and then yesterday he said again that he didn't pass by the school on that second day. So he's changed his statement again. So I'm not going to ask any more questions about this. If the Prosecution thinks that this is not correct, they should say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness has made it clear that the statement he made during the course of the proofing session may have gotten somewhere lost in the translation. He explained that. He explained that he passed by the school twice, and perhaps there was a misunderstanding through the translation. And I think that's fair. I don't think we can really draw anything further from that, and I don't think this would be an appropriate time to make an argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And, Mr. Stojanovic, please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. All I wanted to do is to show that the testimony of the witness had been changed many times and there are constant translation problems. Could the usher help us to show the witness Exhibit P225 [as interpreted]. This is a Prosecution exhibit. And could the Prosecution perhaps provide a B/C/S version. We have a sufficient number of copies in English. This is 525, P525. You have it in our list; it's the report from the state security. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, please pay attention to the last paragraph. It's a document from the Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior, the state security sector. And it is a report being forwarded to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Unfortunately I don't have a copy because the only copy we have now given to Mr. Stojanovic and the witness. Perhaps we can -- I guess we have now put it on the ELMO. But I assume there's no other extra copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've got enough copies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the last paragraph it says: "Early in the morning of the 15th of July, a group of about 100 prisoners, Muslim prisoners from Srebrenica managed to escape from Gornja Pilica in the Zvornik municipality." Mr. Petrovic, we've had the opportunity of hearing Mr. Ruez's testimony here, an investigator in the Srebrenica case, and he spoke about information about shooting in front of the Kula school, shooting directed at the prisoners who had been brought there. I have just shown you this report from the state security of the Republika Srpska Ministry of the Interior. Do you know anything about this event?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the shooting in front of the school?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 15th, were you informed, either in Zvornik or in Pilica, of such an incident?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours, but the witness has told me that he hasn't heard the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone tell you in Zvornik, because you said you went to the Zvornik municipality, or in Pilica, did anyone tell you about this incident that occurred a day or a night before?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I was on the 15th, I can't be sure whether I was there on that date because I was in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know anything about this event?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally don't know anything about this event, but -- I wasn't there, so how could I know about it? As for the event at the Kula school, I've told you about that, but I don't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday when asked by the Prosecution, you said that on the 15th you also gave bread to prisoners in the cultural centre in Pilica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that I can't provide you with the exact dates. It's a little confusing, but yesterday I said - and I didn't mention any dates - I said when the prisoners arrived I went to take bread with someone. But whether it was on the 15th, I don't know. All of this happened around the 12th, that's what I'm saying. I can't say whether it was on the 11th or on the 12th or on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So could we then agree that it was one day after the prisoners had arrived, or rather, the first day that they arrived in the cultural centre in Pilica?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just like to remind you once again on the statement you gave about the prisoners in 1992. On that occasion you said that you had organised a supply of bread for those prisoners, and you said that a military officer or someone in charge in the Territorial Defence, Mr. Pavlovic told you that you should not get involved and that this was not your concern. Now in 1995, the situation happened again. You gave the prisoners bread, you organised the supply of bread, and someone from the Zvornik Brigade command told you once more that this was not your concern. You used the same words. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doesn't it seem to be a bit odd to you that when prisoners had come to the local commune in which you are the president, on both occasions you organised the supply of bread and someone else tells you that this is not your concern. When the same situation is repeated and the same words are used. Is that what happened, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they repeated the exact words, but I said I couldn't quote exactly what someone told me in 1992. But the gist of what the person said was what you said, but I can't remember the exact words used by someone at the time. I didn't make an effort and I wasn't able to tell The Hague investigator exactly what someone told me in 1992 and 1995. But I told them what my understanding had been of the situation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've tried to quote from your statement. I have it in front of you. I think I was clear about that, but the substance of what you said is that on both occasions when you as the president of the local commune, as the most responsible person in the local commune, when you asked what was going on and you organised the supply of bread, on that occasion someone else told you that was not your concern. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You have come to this conclusion. You're correct. Someone else told me that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, is it possible that you as the person in the position of highest authority as the president of the local commune, on the 16th or on some other day when there were so many civilians in your local commune, is it possible for you to say that you were at home and that you slept through this?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's quite possible when prisoners of war were concerned. And I think perhaps it was a Saturday or a Sunday, and perhaps it was because a month earlier I had a death in my family and I didn't have a permanent post in my office. And it's possible that if the citizens needed something, they could find me at home. And also during that period, I was supposed to be assigned to a war unit in the Zvornik Brigade in the Nisici plateau. I said that I was returned home. So when I was at home and there were such situations in Pilica, I wouldn't be present. I came to this conclusion because there were prisoners of war, so even if I wanted to I couldn't have changed anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, this is what we are trying to demonstrate, it's because you didn't want to be present. To justify why you weren't there, you used the words: Go home. It's not your problem. These are words used in 1992 when the prisoners from Djulici came and these are words that were used in 1995 when prisoners from Srebrenica came. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, but I said I can't say exactly what someone told me. That was my understanding. That's what I understood had been said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Naturally I don't expect you to reproduce the exact words used, but we're in a very difficult situation because of these words. And That's why I'm saying that you said that this was on the whole correct. You were told in 1992 and 1995 that you should not get involved, that this was no business of yours, and you were the president of the local commune. And according to the statute of the local commune, you were the person in the position of highest authority at the time. This all took place in the basement of your office? Am I correct? Mr. Petrovic, you were up on the floor and this all took place in the basement of your office.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. First of all, this is not correct to say that this was on the base of the statute, that the president in the local commune presides and cooperates with third parties -- well, those are the responsibilities according to the statute as far as I know. He doesn't preside over the council of the local commune in the sense that he implements the decisions of the local commune and has authority to cooperate with, as they say, third parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's correct. You are the president of the local commune council, and you were the person who has to implement decisions of the council of the local commune?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
