utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't see how anyone else could have more responsibility than the president of the local commune, and this is contained in the statute. But let's return to the 16th or some other date that you cannot remember now.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were at home, if I have understood you correctly, on that day and you don't know what was happening in the killing fields of Branjevo and the cultural centre. But on the 17th when you arrived you said that you had seen a lorry that was transporting bodies from the cultural centre in Pilica together with soldiers, escorted by soldiers. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct to say that this vehicle was a Raba lorry and Djordjic Radivoje, your acquaintance was driving it?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you what kind of vehicle it was, I can't distinguish them, but whether Radivoje was the driver, I don't know. I don't know whether Radivoje Djordjic was the driver. I didn't say that I passed by there. I couldn't see who was inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, one witness has testified here, has provided a statement to the Prosecution. I didn't think it necessary to show this document. If necessary, I will. But I just want to remind you that this witness appeared and he was to monitor the machines involved in the harvest. And he said he saw tractors and elderly people from the local commune who were involved in the transport and burial of the victims. Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about this. I can't confirm it and I can't deny it and I can't say that it's true or not. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct to say that in Branjevo in the activity of burying these people, the local commune and the police participated in this activity?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I correct to say that you personally participated in organising the burial?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to help us again. You're under oath here. Tell this Trial Chamber who participated, who was involved in the burials on the 17th in Pilica or on some other day. Help us solve this issue.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement, if it's been correctly translated, I said I saw a number of people there who were -- walking around Pilica who were present in Pilica. And that was an inhabited place where the army would go. They would come from the field, come on leave. There were citizens going to the post office, the shops, and so on. There were people in uniform, so I don't know what positions these people had. I don't know what their duties were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, do you know that within the Zvornik Brigade there was an R or reserve battalion?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as far as I know, this was a reserve battalion that had soldiers who would be involved in work and they would join military units when necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that these were mostly elderly people, not the first -- not soldiers involved in active duty?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have information, but I'm not sure. I said the reserve battalion was composed of people who had work obligations, regardless of their age, et cetera. They would be mobilised when it was necessary for the unit. I don't know how people were mobilised into that unit -- into those units, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the indictment, which is a basic document for us, it says - I'll paraphrase - that members of the R Battalion, of the Zvornik Brigade, transported bodies from the cultural centre in Pilica to the killing fields in Branjevo. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we talk about -- when we discuss the battalion, we're talking about these people, but I think there was some work platoons in the battalions, in the units. But I don't know the entire procedure now; I don't know exactly who did what. They were in these lower units, these work platoons. I know some colleagues who were involved in work; they had work obligations. They would sometimes send them into combat; that's how I know about this. But the main purpose of the R Battalion, I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the question was: Was it possible, and would you say that it's correct, that what is stated in the indictment is correct, that members of the R Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade were involved in this?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then I will ask you: Could representatives or members of the local commune of Pilica have been involved in this who were organised in the civilian protection or in some other manner, could they have done this within the local commune?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could they have done it within that framework, the units of civilian protection? The staff, the municipal staff of the civilian protection -- well, the members of the civilian protection, they couldn't have done this if someone wasn't mobilised into the army from the civilian protection. At that time, I as the president of the local commune, didn't know exactly when someone was a member of the civilian protection. I didn't even have about 70 per cent -- it didn't exist for about 70 per cent of the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to understand, also in view of the interpretation that we received, is it possible that members of the civil protection from the Pilica local commune took part in this. Can you say yes or no or I don't remember or if you can give us our comment on this.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you mean when you say "in this."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the process of burial, that is the removal of the bodies and the burial of the bodies, the bodies from the Pilica cultural centre and the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the programme of the civil protection is concerned, it's very difficult for me to explain to you how it was organised. I'm not ruling out the possibility that this was the case, but I really don't know anything about it. There are different various units of the civil protection service. There is the fire brigade, the flood emergency brigade, and to be frank, I've never heard of a unit which would have been in charge of burial. I don't remember that this was part of the civil protection programme. Each civil protection or civil defence unit had its -- their programme. I don't remember having a unit which would have been specifically in charge of burials.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the term asanacija or the mopping up unit which would have been part of the civil protection department?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with such a unit. It's possible that the Zvornik Territorial Defence had a unit to that effect, yes, but I don't know. I'm not familiar with this term as far as the local commune is concerned. In my capacity as the president of the local community, I was unaware of that. I was never informed of any such procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, as far as the entire operation is concerned, the burial and the transport of bodies, did you see any machines such as tractors taking part in this operation?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Let me clarify. I never saw any burial. I was never present at Branjevo. I was not aware of that, and I am not aware of any machines taking part in such a burial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have an opportunity to see any construction machine, either present at Branjevo or moving in the direction of Branjevo?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, for the purposes of our case, can you help us with the following: When exactly, at what time, did you see Slavko Peric on that day, when he told you that those were war prisoners? At what time of the day could it have taken place?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, maybe sometime before noon in the morning hours. It was summertime; it was already very warm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? At about what hour in the morning?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 10.00 or 11.00, thereabouts. Again, I don't remember the exact time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, why am I asking this? We intend to examine a witness that has been announced to appear shortly who talked about the composition of the security service within the Zvornik Brigade. And we are interested in this particular detail, because this witness will testify about these events. Is it possible that you did not have contact with Slavko Peric? This witness says that the security officer was at the command of the Zvornik Brigade. Slavko Peric does not mention the fact that he talked to you. Do you still abide by what you said? You are under oath. Are you still telling us that a conversation with Slavko Peric did indeed take place and that it was Slavko Peric who informed you of the imminent arrival of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I remember having talked to Slavko. The only thing I'm not sure about is the exact hour and the date. Again, it was sometime around St. Peter's Day and prior to the arrival of the detainees. That's all I can say. Well, if the Chamber needs to know, I will try to talk to other witnesses to establish when that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have a Prosecution exhibit to that effect and a testimony of a witness to that effect as to how Jovic happened to find himself at the force engineers' unit when he issued certain orders. This does not tell you the times that you mentioned. Mr. Petrovic, is it still your testimony that you had a conversation with Dragan Jovic about the man present here in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I already told you that I had been in Sepak and that I had discussed the issue at the brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the last sentence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that he introduced himself as Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that it is possible that the person present here in the courtroom, Dragan Jokic, may not have been the man with whom you had had this conversation?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, from what I am able to tell as far as the voice is concerned, it was him. However, I'm not ruling out the possibility that it was not him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the purposes of the interpretation and the record, the last sentence: You are not ruling out the possibility that it was not Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can repeat the whole thing or I can repeat the last sentence. He was introduced to me as Dragan Jokic, duty officer. And I was convinced on the basis of our telephone conversation that it was Dragan Jokic. But I'm not ruling out the possibility that it was someone else. I'm testifying about what I believe to be true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Let me conclude with a couple of questions that I wish to clear up with you and concern your testimony yesterday. Where was the key of the local commune when the soldier came to see you to ask for the key on that day?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had the key of the local commune, and no one asked me for that key.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the community centre or the youth centre key?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The youth centre key was with an Agroprom employee who had accommodation there, which is the reason why he had the key.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I right if I say that normally the key was at the local commune?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not. All these facilities are in the -- are the property of the Agroprom company. I raised the issue of the ownership at a couple of meetings, and the Municipal Assembly finally allocated the community centre to the local commune, but not everything has been arranged, administratively speaking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't understand. When was the ownership of this community centre transferred to the local commune and when was it the property of Agroprom?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I raised the issue of its ownership while I was a deputy. I'm not aware of the existence of any evidence to that effect, but there must be a decision of the municipality to that effect, that is, that all such facilities would be transferred to the local commune. And this was the case with the Pilica community centre, but it was only this year that we were able to collect any money from that -- it was only this year that it became our property.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to understand. In July 1995 the Pilica community centre was the property of Agroprom and not the Pilica local commune?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We did not understand the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As to who had the keys, we don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, would you please repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, at the time of the events, Agroprom had the keys, or rather, one of their employees who was in charge of that. And since he -- since they had the keys, they were the owner of this facility. In other words, the local commune could not have the keys, let alone myself. There was an employee of Agroprom who was in charge of that, who was in possession of those keys.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that a man wearing military uniform came to see you and ask for the key. Can you just tell us at what time that was.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in the evening hours, towards the end of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the evening hours, would that be after 6.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the evening, perhaps a little earlier than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At nightfall in summertime, that would have been then at 2000. But is it possible that it took place at 6.00 p.m.?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but it was around that time. I can talk in terms of time of the day, but the exact hour I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I couldn't agree more, Mr. Petrovic. But these hours are very important for us because there are certain indications as to the exact time when those people were brought to the Pilica community centre. But let me turn to a question that was raised yesterday. You said that on that day you had gone to the town hall to take care of things having to do with the mobilisation, or rather, the demobilisation of a member of the Zvornik Brigade. What was the procedure that was normally applied in -- to demobilisation when you wanted to have members of the brigade be used for the purposes of the harvest?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was customary for the local commune to submit a list of people to the municipality, a list of people who owned a combine. And such a list was always sent to the commission which was in charge of the harvest. I think that the request was then sent to the Ministry of the Defence, and then the Ministry of the Defence sent a memo to that effect to the brigade command, which in turn would forward it to the battalion command. And then it was the battalion commander who took the final decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was the brigade command which needed the support of the battalion command, but this all went through the Ministry for Defence?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the other way around. It was the local commune that sent such a request to the municipal commission which, I assume, would turn to the Zvornik branch of the Ministry of Defence, who would then contact the battalion command -- or rather, the brigade command. And it was the commander who then decided whether so-and-so would be released or demobilised for this purpose. That was my understanding of the procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The request originates from the local commune, and you went the whole circle, via the Ministry of Defence, the brigade command the battalion command -- or rather, the unit, the command of the unit under whose jurisdiction the relevant member was?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who this soldier was whom you requested to be demobilised for the purposes of the harvest?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lazar Rakic, who came to me on that day. I had a list of people who owned a combine, but I didn't have his name on my list. So he came to see me to tell me that and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as paragraph 51 of the indictment is concerned, let me ask you if you were familiar with any reburial activity?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I personally don't have any knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the bodies were removed from the Branjevo Military Farm?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean if I'm aware? Me personally?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You personally.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I saw that or heard that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, or if you have any knowledge to that effect.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The microphone is not working. No I didn't see any such activity take place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that the bodies were removed?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I heard stories to that effect, but I didn't believe them, or rather, I personally didn't know about that. But I did hear rumours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, those bodies were indeed removed from the area taken to the so-called secondary burial site, and this is a well-known fact. Finally let me ask you: Your answers to the effect that you know nothing about what happened on the 14th, the 15th, the 16th, or any other date, and about the events involving burial of the bodies only show your effort to minimise the role that you as the president of the local commune had at the time.

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was the president of the local commune, but I was absent one evening, one whole day, one evening, and then the following day until noon. And this is what I stated in my statement. Saturday, Saturday evening, Sunday, Sunday morning. When I -- at the time I was giving my statement, I said I would need a calendar to establish the exact days, but I remember that I spent one evening, one whole day, and one morning at home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stojanovic, I think many questions have been asked and answered many times. I hope you could wind up your cross-examination as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have actually concluded my cross-examination. I do not wish to take up any of the Court's time any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any redirect? Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Just one question, Your Honour, thank you. Re-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you know whether or not Mr. Jokic was a member of any political parties before or during the war?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if Mr. Jokic was at any time a member of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: PERO PETROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. I don't know all members of the SDS, so I don't know. I'm sorry, that's the only answer I can give you. I don't know whether he was a member of the SDS. I cannot remember -- at least while I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Ms. Issa?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes, there are. We will be tendering the following, Your Honour: P17.2, P666 and 667.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. To my understanding, that document P17.2 has already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: My understanding, Your Honour, was that it was referred to in Mr. Ruez's evidence, however it had not been admitted at that point. I don't believe it was tendered. Perhaps it was missed. But that's the information I have, so I'm seeking to have it tendered at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And I have a question concerning the documents P666 and 67. Are there any marks by this witness on that map?

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, there are no marks. The witness simply referred to particular places, particular street -- not street, but a particular town on the map which was not visible or perhaps was not present on other maps that we have tendered in the past. I think it was Tisic [phoen], if I recall correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections to these two exhibits, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think three exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we accept that the number 17 has not yet been admitted, then, yes, the same goes for that particular one. We have no objections to these three exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. These three exhibits are admitted into the evidence. Are there any documents on your part, Mr. Stojanovic, to tender at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We have used the same three exhibits which we used during the examination of Mr. Butler, so we do not have documents to tender. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home. During the break, the usher will show you out of the room. It's time for a break and we'll resume at quarter to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good evening, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Ms. Davis.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Ms. Davis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good evening, Witness. I wanted to start by asking you a couple of questions about our meeting the other day. Do you remember meeting with me and with an investigator in our offices on Monday of this week?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And during that meeting, we advised you of your right to remain silent and to have a lawyer present during the interview to represent you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: A lawyer is not necessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's right. And at that time you waived your rights and you agreed to speak to us without a lawyer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also agreed to testify in court today without a lawyer. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to inform you that as you can see there's a screen around you and that for the purposes of any video of these proceedings that's going to the outside world, your face is being distorted, so you're protected in that sense. My understanding is you are comfortable with having your name used during these proceedings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can use my name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would you please state your name and spell your name for the record.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: My name is M-i-t-r-o-v-i-c, that's the last name; and M-i-l-o-s.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mitrovic, can you please tell us your nationality.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I am a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you joined the Bosnian Serb army in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And with which unit were you affiliated when you first joined the VRS in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: First I was in the civilian police. And afterwards -- well, I was for six months in the civilian police. And later on, I was a member of the military police for about two months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the military police unit with which you were affiliated attached to a brigade of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: In the battalion of the military police, I was in Petkovci.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that attached also to a brigade or not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you became a member of the Zvornik Brigade engineering company?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think it was in December, towards the end of December, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In which year?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did it come to pass that you were transferred from the military police to the engineering company of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were six of us in the military police in Petkovci and three died in Klisa, three remained. So I was at home after that. I went there. I reported to the command, and they said I should wait. So after that, Captain Jokic and Milan Mijatovic appeared. They asked me to go to the engineering company. They said that they had to mobilise people. They had a few Muslims that had been left when they went to Subotica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to back up for a moment. You mentioned that Captain Jokic and I believe you said Mijatovic came to see you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "Captain Jokic," which Captain Jokic are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I am referring to Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us one more time what Captain Jokic and Mijatovic told you when they came to visit you.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: They told me -- they asked me whether I could go to the engineering unit. They said they would mobilise Skip because he was with me and he was needed for the engineering unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Am I to understand that you were in possession of a Skip?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did you gain possession of the Skip that you had?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, this neighbour Muslim, when they were supposed to go to Subotica, he asked me whether he could leave that machine with me. When they returned, I was to return it to them. I agreed and took the machine home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Captain Jokic came to you. Where were you when he came to you with Mr. Mijatovic? I'm not sure if Mr. Mijatovic is around.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I was at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Captain Jokic and Mijatovic came to you and told you that they had to mobilise the machine. And what were you told, if anything, with respect to your obligations?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, they said I should go with the machine. I said I wasn't very well trained because I had never operated such machines. They said that wasn't a problem, that there would be a machinist up there, and I would receive training from him. That's how I went to the engineers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've referred to the machine as a Skip. Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what the machine looks like that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: That was a Torpedo machine. It had rubber on it and it was like -- it had tyres like a tractor. It had a bucket for loading and behind it had a small bucket for digging canals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were two buckets on the Skip?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do I understand that one of the buckets was in the front and one in the back?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I would ask the usher's assistance in showing to the witness an exhibit that has been marked P354. This is, in fact, the second page of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could, using the pointer that the usher is handing to you, could you tell us - and I'm afraid the edge of the exhibit seems to be cut off slightly - could you tell us whether any of the machinery that's depicted on this exhibit resembles the Skip that you're describing.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which one, if you could point to it, is that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're pointing to the upper right diagram. Thank you. What colour was this Skip that belonged to your neighbour that was mobilised at the request of Captain Jokic and Mr. Mijatovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: It was yellow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it in working order?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After you joined the engineering company and the Skip was mobilised, was the Skip then used by the engineering company in the course of its duties?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long was the Skip used by the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: For about three months I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who operated the Skip during this period?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Me and Cvijetin Ristanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me where the skip was stored when it was not in use during this period.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: In the base, in the youth settlement in Karakaj, in the youth centre, youth area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mention a youth settlement in Karakaj. What was that? How did that relate to the engineering company, if it did?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: There were barracks there for the youth actions. When they worked in Zvornik and Tuzla, and this is where the people who were involved in these actions were provided with accommodation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you mentioned that this was the -- you've mentioned a base and then the youth settlement. Is the base what was used by the Zvornik Brigade engineering company as its compound?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's where we were positioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned that the Skip was used by the engineering company for three months. What happened after three months?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: After three months later, the motor left and then Captain Jokic said I could take the machine home and that I should tow it there and leave it, at home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning your attention to July of 1995, were you still a member of the Zvornik Brigade engineering company at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you a member of a platoon within the brigade -- within the company?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which one was that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: That was the transport platoon and fortification platoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the duties of the fortification platoon, generally?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it had to cobble roads, dig canals, dig communicating trenches, and the like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was your commander in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: You mean the platoon commander?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can start with the platoon commander, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: It was Damjan Lazarevic; he was the platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the chain of command above Mr. Lazarevic at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: There was Dragan Jevtic; he was the company commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: The chief of the engineers, Captain Jokic, Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from whom did you take orders in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I took orders from the company commander or from the platoon commander or from the chief of the engineers, Commander Jokic, if he was present.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In July of 1995, did you have any particular machinery to which you -- that you were assigned to operate as the member of the fortification platoon?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: There was the Skip that was mobilised from Glinica from the tactical group Birac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this the same Skip to which you were referring before, or is this a different Skip?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: The same one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is the one from your Muslim neighbour or a different -- I should have been more specific when I said "before."

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, a different one that was mobilised from the company in Glinica, TG Birac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what brand was this Skip from Birac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Torpedo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the description of this Torpedo Skip essentially the same as the description of the Skip that you've told us about that you had obtained from your Muslim neighbour?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it accurate to say that the diagram on the upper right corner of the exhibit to your left on the ELMO also is similar to the Skip that you operated in July 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was the Skip mobilised from Birac, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when it was mobilised, but it was mobilised when necessary, when it was necessary to carry out work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1995, with what sort of frequency was the Skip being used by the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: It was used often, because it was necessary for repairing the roads, for digging canals. So it was mostly with us in the engineers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "with you in the engineers," was it stored -- where was it stored when it wasn't in use in the summer of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: It was in the barracks in a Latin school settlement where we were deployed. It was in the warehouses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the engineering compound that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be helpful if you could briefly describe the engineering compound for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, there were some warehouses there where we were deployed. There was a facility where the command was located, another one where we would sleep. And there was a canteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the officers and the enlisted men in the engineering compound sleep in the same facility or in separate facilities -- buildings I should say.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: In separate ones.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was -- you mentioned a command building. What was in the command building?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: The chief of engineers was there, the company commander, the platoon commanders, the commanders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any sleeping facilities for enlisted men in the command building?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like now to turn your attention more specifically to the 13th of July, 1995. Can you tell us what duties you were engaged in on the 13th of July.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: On the 13th of July, we were down there where the facilities were located. The chief of engineers, Jokic, I don't know whether he ordered Dragan Jevtic and the soldiers who were available to take all their military equipment to go to Standard and to join -- we should join the logistical unit there. And we were told that we would go -- that we should go to Snagovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what time of day did you receive word that you were to go to Standard and join the logistics unit and then go to Snagovo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I think that was about 10.00 or 11.00, but I'm not quite certain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from whom did you actually receive the instruction to gather your belongings and get ready to go to Standard?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: From Jevtic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you mentioned that you were told that you were to go to Standard and join the logistics unit, and then that you would go to Snagovo. Is that, in fact, what you then did?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you told by Jevtic what you would be doing there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were told that there would be a big column of Muslims from Srebrenica and that we should go up to Snagovo in order to direct people, to prevent them from going to the town, to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "to direct people to prevent them from going to the town," do you mean the column of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many members of the engineering company were mobilised to go to Snagovo on the 13th of July with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I think about 15 of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any officers accompanying you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Dragan Jevtic accompanied us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived in Snagovo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: When the lorries took us there, we went out into the field. And we took up position along the combat line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were your duties there on the combat line?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, our duties were to direct the column of Muslims, to prevent them from heading towards Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "direct the column of Muslims"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that they knew where they were to go, and this was to prevent the column from dispersing and to enable them to go towards the elevation they were heading towards, to make it possible for them to pass through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any interaction with the column of Muslims while you were at Snagovo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long were you there at Snagovo on the line?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I stayed there from the 13th until the 14th in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Aside from Jevtic who accompanied you, did you see any other officers of the Zvornik Brigade while you were at Snagovo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: In the morning of the 14th at about 4.00 a.m., Major Dragan Obrenovic came by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when Obrenovic came by?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, nothing in particular. He just passed by, by our lines, and continued on his way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you left the line at Snagovo on the 14th. About what time was it that you left?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was sometime in the afternoon, at about 3.00 or 4.00 p.m. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did it come to pass that you left the line?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were informed through the radio communications that we should report to Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Myself and Miladinovic. The two of us were supposed to report at Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is Miladinovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: He was also one of the construction machine operators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that you were informed through the radio communications that you should report to Orahovac. How did you actually receive the message that you were to report at Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was Dragan Markovic who was told by the communications people what to do. He conveyed the message to Jevtic, the commander, who told us that we should report and that we should come back with the trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what trucks are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: The trucks that had brought reinforcement to the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that Miladinovic was another machine operator. Was he from your -- from the engineering company also?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what types of machines did Mr. Miladinovic operate for the engineering company?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: He operated a bulldozer and an excavator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the 15 men from the engineering company who had been sent to Snagovo with you, were there any other machine operators, aside from you and Miladinovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who sent the order that was conveyed to you through Markovic and Jevtic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your reaction when you received the order that you should report to Orahovac?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, we were confused, because we didn't know what was going on. We were also afraid, because we were not aware of the reasons why we were now being sent back from the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone else from the engineering company accompany you when you left, aside from Miladinovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Jevtic remained at Snagovo when you left?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you and Miladinovic go?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: We went back to the base, to the facilities there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report to anyone when you returned to the compound?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We reported to Slavko Bogicevic, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is Slavko Bogicevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: He was the officer in charge of morale for the force engineers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any other officers present when you reported back to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember, but I think that Damjan Lazarevic was there; however, I'm not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you returned to the base and reported to Bogicevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: When we reported to Bogicevic, he said that Miladinovic should go with them in a TAM truck and that I should remain at the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "with them," do you mean with Bogicevic or with others?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Bogicevic went, accompanied by the TAM truck driver, Mr. Miladinovic, so the three of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know where they were going?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Bogicevic indicate to you and Miladinovic when you came back anything about where he was -- where Miladinovic was being sent?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When Miladinovic left -- well, did Miladinovic then leave with Bogicevic and the driver of the TAM truck?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I stayed at the compound in the dormitory of the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for how long did you stay there in the dormitory of the compound?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I spent the night there on the 14th, and I spent the entire day of the 15th. And again, I spent the night at the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the evening of the 14th, did you see Miladinovic or Bogicevic again?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the 15th of July, did you receive any orders or instructions on the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that you were at the compound the entire day of the 15th and spent the night there on the 15th. Who else was at the compound that you saw?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: You mean on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Almost nobody -- Vojislav Sekanic was, I think, there at the command, together with a guard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where on the compound did you spend the day on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: In one of the huts there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "huts"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is where the dormitories were; this is where we slept. I slept in one of the dormitories there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the command building at all on the 15th?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the 16th of July, can you tell us whether you received any orders on that day.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the orders that you received?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: At about 8.00 or 9.00, I don't know the exact time, the force engineers' commander, Dragan Jokic, arrived, and he told me that I should go to Kozluk with the Skip, together with Nikola Rikanovic. That I should report there to Damjan Lazarevic, that he would be waiting for us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you when Dragan Jokic came and told you to report with the Skip to Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I was at the base in the dormitory, at the compound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did Mr. Jokic tell you where you were supposed to find Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: He told us to go there to the mineral water factory Vitinka and that Damjan would meet us somewhere on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Jokic tell you what you would be doing when you met Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: He didn't say what we would be doing. He just said that Damjan would be waiting for us, and that he would give us the instructions as to what we would be doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned earlier that Lazarevic was your platoon commander. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Jevtic still at Snagovo at this point?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Jevtic's absence, to whom did Lazarevic, as platoon commander, report?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: You mean when we came back from the tasking or --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. More generally, setting aside this particular day. If Jevtic was unavailable or in the field, to whom would a platoon commander report in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: To the force engineers' commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us what happened when you arrived in Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: When we arrived in Kozluk, Damjan Lazarevic was waiting for us at the road. He told me to step down from the vehicle, so I got out. And he told me to come along to see what should be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was Lazarevic -- did you find Lazarevic where you had been told you would find him by Mr. Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He waited for us on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did Lazarevic take you after you got down from the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: He took us along a path leading to the Drina, on the right side of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did you see when he took you along this path?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Once we got there, I saw bodies of people that had been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "bodies of people that had been killed," can you give us an estimate of how many bodies you saw there.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you how many, because the area was covered with holes from which sand and pebble stone were excavated. But one could sense the smell already hanging in the air, but it's difficult to tell how many there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mention that the area was covered with holes. Were the bodies in the holes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how many holes did you see that had bodies inside?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: There were two to three such locations. I don't remember exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How large were the holes across, in terms of metres?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember. They were not very large, though.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise for asking these difficult questions, but were the bodies that you saw lying in the holes lying on top of one another or was it one layer of bodies?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: They were laying on top of one another. There were no layers of bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you see any -- what type of clothing the corpses had on them?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I could see, civilian clothing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you able to identify any wounds or any evidence of how the bodies -- how the people had been killed?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. I was not, because they must have been killed sometime ago. It was not possible to get closer to the bodies to see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to clarify, who was with you at this point when you were viewing the bodies in the pits?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Damjan Lazarevic and Nikola Rikanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after they showed you where these bodies were?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, he told me to put earth on top of the bodies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I assume that was with the Torpedo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you work with the Torpedo covering the bodies with earth?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I worked for about half an hour, then the ULT-220 arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the ULT-220?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: It's a kind of loader with rubber tyres, a type of excavator used for loading things and trucks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning again to the exhibit that is still next to you on the ELMO, Exhibit P354, can you tell us whether you see anything on -- any diagram depicted there that looks like the ULT-220 or the type of machine that the ULT-220 was.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: If we can have the assistance of the usher --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's not here.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I believe only a portion of the exhibit is shown at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're pointing to the bottom left drawing on the exhibit, for the record?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, who brought the ULT-220 to Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Rade Boskovic did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who is Rade Boskovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: He used to work at Josanica. He was in charge of loading.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he work at Josanica in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know where he worked at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what Josanica is.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Josanica is a quarry where stone is excavated for the purposes of road construction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this ULT-220, did it belong to the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To whom did it belong?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: It belonged to the Josanica company, and when necessary it was commandeered for the needs of the Zvornik Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the old 220 had been, to your knowledge, by the Zvornik Brigade engineering company on previous occasions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, when necessary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand the question correctly, it was a leading one. That is, that the machine had been used for the needs of the Zvornik Brigade. That's not what the witness said. The witness said that it had been mobilised for the needs of the Zvornik Brigade -- I mean, it was not mobilised for the needs of the Zvornik Brigade engineering company. The witness only mentioned the Zvornik Brigade, and that's not one and the same thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Davis, maybe you could ask some questions to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you mentioned that the ULT belonging to the Josanica company had been commandeered for the needs of the Zvornik Brigade, to which -- for the needs of which unit, if any, was the ULT-220 commandeered?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Force engineers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why the Boskovic arrived at Kozluk with the ULT-220?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact reasons why he came to assist me, because they knew that this machine was not properly working and that I would not be able to finish the work. And that was the reason why this other machine was being sent, I guess.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. When you mention the machine that was not properly working, which machine are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: To the Torpedo, the Skip.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was wrong with the Torpedo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: The hydraulic system wasn't working properly, and then the machine itself was not strong enough for major work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned that they knew that the machine wasn't working properly. To whom were you referring when you said "they knew"?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: The command of the force engineers, the chief force engineer. They all knew that the machine was not in perfect working condition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What happened when Boskovic arrived at the site at Kozluk with the ULT-220?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: He continued with covering the bodies with earth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he arrive and immediately begin doing that, or were there any conversations between any of the people that were present?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I just think that he said hello that Damjan and started working.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, then, that he knew what he was to do when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation. She has been leading slightly. Now she's speculating or asking the witness to speculate. I think that she -- if she rephrases, we can all derive a particular conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I would be happy to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Boskovic appear to know what he was to do when he arrived at the site?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. No, he didn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how did he learn what he was to do?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, probably because he reported to Damjan. He went up to Damjan, and it was Damjan who told him what he was to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After Boskovic began assisting with the ULT-220, did you keep working with the Torpedo as well?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, I stopped. I moved to the side, because there was no need for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long were you there at the site at Kozluk after Boskovic arrived?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: For about an hour, an hour and a half. I don't know exactly how long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you go when you left the site?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: You mean after we had finished the work, as we were going back?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. After you finished the work.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: After we had finished the work, Damjan told us to go back to the base in Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With whom did you travel back to the base in Karakaj?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: With Nikola Rikanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how long did it take you to get back there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Between 40 and 45 minutes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any discussion with Rikanovic in the vehicle as you were driving back to the base?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. I felt bad. We didn't talk about anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do when you returned to the base or the engineering compound?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I returned there. I left the machine there. Damjan Lazarevic went with us, and he said we could go home, that we were free.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you left the machine, and did you immediately go home or ...

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As soon as Damjan appeared and said we could go home, as soon as he said that we were free, yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did Damjan return to the base with you in the same vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you see Damjan arrive back at the base when you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, I went to the dormitory. I went to the bathroom, washed my hands and my face, and then Damjan appeared after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you required to report to anyone when you returned, generally, when you returned from a job?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: We weren't required because -- to do so, because the platoon commander was there and it wasn't necessary for us to report, since the reports would be relayed containing information about what had been done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know whether Damjan, in fact, relayed any report about what had been done?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you returned to the base and you went to the barracks. And how long thereafter did Damjan appear to tell you that you could have the day off?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I think about 10 or 15 minutes later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know why you were given the day off?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know why, probably because we didn't have any particular duties at the time. Damjan told us that we could go home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would -- well, do you recall when we met in our offices a couple of days ago looking at excerpts from the Zvornik Brigade engineering vehicle logs?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you just a couple of those excerpts now and ask you a couple of questions about them.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: If the usher could provide the witness with Exhibit P516 and the B/C/S version is /B, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it. It's a transport order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us which vehicle this is -- this document is for.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: It is for a Torpedo excavator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the Skip to which you were referring earlier, the Torpedo Skip?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You can see on the middle of the right-hand side of the first page that your name appears with the name of Mr. Ristanovic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me what that signifies, the fact that your names appear there on this vehicle log.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it means that we were the operators of the vehicle, and it also concerns fuel needs and it also states what was done where.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Trial Chamber the -- how the fuel needs were logged, that you just referred to, on these documents.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, they would take account of the consumption and the number of hours worked. As they knew how much fuel the vehicle would consume, they would keep a record of the fuel used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, and who makes -- who was responsible in July of 1995 for making the entries of the fuel used?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a form that you, as an operator, would fill in?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't fill it in. At the beginning when we received the fuel up in Standard, we would fill in these transport orders and fill in the information on the amount of fuel required. But later on, we didn't do this. They would bring in the fuel in canisters and fill up the vehicle with the amount that was needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could turn to the next page of this exhibit. You'll note that there is an entry on the right-hand side for the 14th of July, 1995, that indicates the vehicle was used from the -- by the VRS and went on a route from the base to Orahovac and return. And the description says: Digging trenches in Orahovac. Do you see where I'm reading?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This machine on the 14th didn't leave the base. It was in Karakaj, but it didn't go to Orahovac at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- and did you go to Orahovac on the 14th?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain why this vehicle log indicates that the vehicle went to Orahovac to dig trenches on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, they probably needed fuel for some other vehicle and they needed a new machine and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to me what you mean by "they needed a new machine."

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the fuel was needed for this machine and it was provided for some other machine that didn't have a transport order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did all of the machines used by the Zvornik Brigade have transport orders?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the next entry on this page is for the 16th of July, 1995, in case the vehicle was used by the VRS and went from Base, Kozluk, to Base. Description: Digging trenches in Kozluk. Does that comport with your recollection of what this vehicle was used for on the 16th of July?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the far right column of the document, second page, still on the second page, in column numbered 20, there are -- would appear to be some signatures, do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who was responsible for signing off on these logs on this page of the -- this entry of this type of log?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: I think it was the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance if the witness can be shown Exhibit P515.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could take a look at this document. Can you tell me which vehicle this log entry is for.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: It's a TAM 75, T-A-M.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, I believe the witness has the wrong exhibit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you now -- if you can look at the -- in the centre of the exhibit, are you looking at P515/B now?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And looking at this document, can you tell me which vehicle this is for.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was an excavator which was defective. I think it was stationed in Josanica and had been defective for several years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, your name and Mr. Ristanovic's name appear on the right-hand side of that page. I assume that has the same significance as it did on the other log, that you were assigned to operate this vehicle. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know -- you say that the vehicle was defective and had been defective for several years. Was it defective and not in working order in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again, looking at the fuel entries just below where your name appears and also at the second page, there appears to be an indication on this document that the vehicle was used at Orahovac on the 14th of July for trench digging. Can you explain that entry.

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't used, because the vehicle was defective and the fuel was probably needed. And it was probably because this excavator had a transport order and it had been registered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just have two final questions for you. Do you know of any investigation by the Army of the Republika Srpska into the murder of the civilians that you were covering with earth at Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge of whether anyone from the Zvornik Brigade or other brigades were ever punished for any involvement in the death of the civilians buried at Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: MILOS MITROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. DAVIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, Witness, I have to remind you, as I did to other witnesses, during your stay in The Hague, do not talk to anybody about your testimony and do not let anybody talk to you about it. Thank you. And we'll resume tomorrow afternoon in the same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
